newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Issing says disappointed with May jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Issing says disappointed with May jobs data.

text.p: Bundesbank Chief Economist Otmar Issing said on Friday the May unemployment data for Germany was "more than disappointing".

The Federal Labour Office said earlier that German unemployment rose 56,000 to a seasonally adjusted 4.358 million in May. The unemployment rate based on unadjusted data fell to 11.1 percent, from 11.3 percent in April.
Issing also said the biggest uncertainity as regards M3 money supply development, a key Bundesbank indicator, was money capital formation, whose volatility was influencing the volatility of M3 data.
"We will have to reckon with the fact that this will continue to be the case," Issing told journalists at a Bundesbank conference in Frankfurt.
Commenting on trends on bank lending volumes, Issing noted that borrowers were taking advantage of the present favourable interest rate environment.
